title: What does FDA's QMSR require for medical device personnel training?
description: What FDA's Quality Management System Regulation requires for device staff competence and training through ISO 13485, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Since February 2, 2026, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Quality Management System Regulation (QMSR), 21 CFR Part 820, requires medical device manufacturers to document a quality management system that complies with ISO 13485:2016, which the rule incorporates by reference. Training and competence therefore follow Clause 6.2 of ISO 13485: FDA says anyone doing work that affects quality must be competent based on appropriate education, training, skills, and expertise, and that this must be carefully recorded.
keyTakeaways: The QMSR took effect on February 2, 2026 and replaced the Quality System (QS) regulation, including its stand-alone training section, former 21 CFR 820.25.

21 CFR 820.10(a) requires a documented quality management system that complies with the applicable requirements of ISO 13485, so personnel competence and training are governed by ISO 13485 Clause 6.2.
FDA's final rule says Clause 6.2 covers internal and external personnel, full-time and part-time staff, contractors, and consultants whose work affects product quality.
Part 820 sets no fixed training interval or minimum hours; the manufacturer decides frequency within its quality management system and must be able to justify it.
Failure to comply renders a device adulterated under section 501(h) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, and an ISO 13485 certificate does not exempt a site from FDA inspection.
regulator: US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Center for Devices and Radiological Health
appliesTo: Manufacturers that design, manufacture, package, label, store, install, or service finished devices intended for human use and marketed in the US, including foreign sites that import or offer devices for import
Contract sterilizers, installers, relabelers, remanufacturers, repackers, specification developers, and initial distributors of foreign entities performing those functions
Internal and external personnel whose work affects product quality, including contractors and consultants
Not component or part manufacturers, which are encouraged but not required to consider the regulation

sections.heading: What is the QMSR and when did it take effect?

blocks.text: The QMSR is the FDA's current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) rule for medical devices, codified at 21 CFR Part 820. According to the [FDA's QMSR page](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/postmarket-requirements-devices/quality-management-system-regulation-qmsr), the rule "is effective February 2, 2026, and is now titled Quality Management System Regulation (QMSR)." It incorporates by reference ISO 13485:2016, Medical devices: Quality management systems: Requirements for regulatory purposes, and Clause 3 of ISO 9000:2015 for vocabulary.

The FDA published the amendments as a [final rule on February 2, 2024](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2024/02/02/2024-01709.txt) (89 FR 7496) with a two-year transition. Its stated aim was to harmonize the US device CGMP framework with the one used by other regulators. This page states the position as at November 2026.

[21 CFR 820.7](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/820.7) names the exact edition: ISO 13485:2016(E), third edition, March 1, 2016. A later revision of ISO 13485 would not change US requirements unless the FDA amends the rule, and the [QMSR FAQ](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/quality-management-system-regulation-qmsr/quality-management-system-regulation-frequently-asked-questions) notes that the incorporated standards can be read in read-only form through the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) incorporated by reference portal.

sections.heading: Where are the training requirements in the QMSR?

blocks.text: The training requirements sit in ISO 13485 itself, not in a dedicated section of Part 820. [21 CFR 820.10(a)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/820.10) requires each manufacturer to "Document a quality management system that complies with the applicable requirements of ISO 13485" and other applicable requirements of Part 820. Subpart B of the [current Part 820](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-H/part-820) adds supplemental provisions only on records (820.35) and labeling and packaging controls (820.45); sections 820.20 to 820.30, where the old personnel and training rules sat, are now reserved.
In the final rule's response to Comment 13, the FDA explained how competence is now covered:

blocks.title: FDA final rule, 89 FR 7496 (Comment 13 response)
blocks.text: "FDA considers Clause 6.2 of ISO 13485 to capture the intent of the previous Sec. 820.75(b)(1) adequately, by requiring that any individuals doing work that impacts quality should be competent on the basis of appropriate education, training, skills, and expertise. Examples of such individuals may include internal and external personnel performing work impacting product quality, full-time and part-time personnel, contractors, and/or consultants. All education, training, skills, and experience of employees need to be carefully recorded."

The same response says the QS regulation's language on qualified and trained personnel for verification and validation (cited by commenters as 820.20(b)(2)) is addressed by Clause 6.2, so the FDA did not carry it into the QMSR. The practical point for training managers: the competence obligation did not shrink. It moved into the standard, and the scope explicitly reaches contractors and consultants.

Clause 6.2 is the competence and training requirement of ISO 13485:2016. Because the standard is paywalled, this page describes it at the level the FDA has described it publicly: personnel performing work affecting product quality must be competent on the basis of appropriate education, training, skills, and experience, and that basis must be recorded.
The FDA's statement contains four elements that a training program has to evidence:

items: **Scope by work, not job title:** anyone whose work affects product quality, which can include engineering, complaint handling, supplier quality, service, and software staff as well as production.
**Competence, not attendance:** the test is whether the person is competent, based on education, training, skills, and experience together.
**People outside the payroll:** contractors, consultants, and external personnel are in scope when their work affects quality.
**Records:** education, training, skills, and experience must be carefully recorded.

blocks.text: Manufacturers should read the full clause text in their licensed copy or the ANSI read-only portal and map each requirement into their procedures. The same competence logic appears in other management system standards, covered in [ISO 9001 competence requirements](/regulations/iso-9001-competence-requirements).

blocks.text: Firms already certified to ISO 13485 will find little new in the training content itself. Firms that only met the old QS regulation need to check their procedures against the standard's clause, not against memory of 820.25.

sections.heading: How often must device personnel be trained under the QMSR?

blocks.text: Part 820 sets no fixed refresher interval or minimum hours, and none appears in the FDA's QMSR page, FAQ, or final rule passages reviewed for this page. Frequency is a quality system decision the manufacturer must make, document, and be ready to justify to an investigator.

Defensible triggers usually include a new hire or role change, a revised procedure or work instruction, a design change, a corrective and preventive action (CAPA) that identifies a training cause, and a periodic refresher set by risk. The final rule notes that the FDA expects a QMSR-adherent system to "identify and correct improper personnel training", which ties training directly into CAPA. For setting intervals, see [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: What will FDA inspectors look at for training?

blocks.text: Inspectors now assess the quality management system against ISO 13485 as incorporated, using a new compliance program. According to the FDA, on February 2, 2026 it "stopped using the Quality System Inspection Technique (QSIT) for device inspections" and began using the inspection process in Compliance Program 7382.850, Inspection of Medical Device Manufacturers.

items: **Broader record access:** the QMSR FAQ states that the FDA can inspect management review, quality audits, and supplier audit reports, and that the exceptions in former 820.180(c) are not maintained. Training gaps raised in internal audits or management review are therefore visible to investigators.
**No certificate shortcut:** the FDA "will not require certificates of conformance to ISO 13485", and a certificate "will not exempt a manufacturer from an FDA inspection."

**Records of competence:** expect requests for role competence requirements, training records linked to procedure versions, qualification of people doing quality-affecting work, and evidence for contractors and consultants.

blocks.text: Preparation steps are in [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) and [how to evidence training effectiveness to a regulator](/guides/how-to-evidence-training-effectiveness-to-a-regulator).

blocks.text: Drug manufacturers follow a different personnel rule, explained in [FDA GMP personnel training (21 CFR 211.25)](/regulations/fda-gmp-personnel-training-requirements). Combination product makers may need to satisfy both.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each QMSR requirement, ISO 13485 clause reference, procedure, and role as linked concepts, then attaches the learning outcomes and assessment points that evidence competence. When a procedure or design changes, the affected roles and assessments are identified from those links. See how this applies in [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Does the QMSR still have a section called Personnel or Training?
faqs.a: No. Former 21 CFR 820.25 was removed, and sections 820.20 to 820.30 are reserved in the current Part 820. Training and competence are governed by ISO 13485 Clause 6.2 through 820.10(a), which requires a quality management system that complies with the applicable requirements of ISO 13485.

faqs.q: Do contractors and consultants need QMSR training records?
faqs.a: Yes, where their work affects product quality. In the final rule, the FDA said individuals covered by Clause 6.2 may include internal and external personnel, full-time and part-time staff, contractors, and consultants, and that education, training, skills, and experience need to be carefully recorded.

faqs.q: Does an ISO 13485 certificate prove QMSR training compliance?
faqs.a: No. The FDA does not require or issue ISO 13485 certificates, and its FAQ states that a certificate will not exempt a manufacturer from an FDA inspection. Investigators review the training system and records directly, and they can now see internal audit and management review reports.

faqs.q: Which version of ISO 13485 applies in the US?
faqs.a: ISO 13485:2016, third edition, dated March 1, 2016, as named in 21 CFR 820.7. Any newer edition would apply in the US only if the FDA amends the regulation to incorporate it.

factCheck.claim: QMSR effective February 2, 2026, now titled Quality Management System Regulation; incorporates by reference ISO 13485:2016 and Clause 3 of ISO 9000:2015; FDA stopped using QSIT on February 2, 2026 and began using Compliance Program 7382.850.

QMSR FAQ: FDA will not require or issue ISO 13485 certificates and a certificate does not exempt a manufacturer from inspection; FDA can inspect management review, quality audits and supplier audit reports, 820.180(c) exceptions not maintained; standards readable via ANSI IBR portal (page updated 11/05/2026).

Final rule (89 FR 7496, February 2, 2024), Comment 13 response: Clause 6.2 requires individuals doing work that impacts quality to be competent on the basis of appropriate education, training, skills, and expertise; examples include internal and external personnel, full and part-time, contractors and consultants; all education, training, skills and experience need to be carefully recorded; former 820.20(b)(2)-type language addressed by Clause 6.2. Also: QMSR-adherent QMS will identify and correct improper personnel training; rule effective February 2, 2026.

820.10(a) requires a documented QMS that complies with applicable ISO 13485 requirements; 820.10(e) failure to comply renders a device adulterated under section 501(h) and the device and responsible person are subject to regulatory action.
820.7(b) incorporates ISO 13485:2016(E), third edition, March 1, 2016, IBR approved for 820.1, 820.3, 820.10, 820.35 and 820.45.

Current Part 820: 820.1 scope (finished devices for human use, foreign manufacturers, components excluded), Subpart B supplemental provisions only at 820.35 and 820.45, 820.20 to 820.30 reserved (checked via eCFR versioner, November 2026).

Former 820.25 text: sufficient personnel with necessary education, background, training and experience; procedures for identifying training needs; training shall be documented; awareness of device defects; verification and validation staff aware of defects and errors. 2024 edition marked effective until 2-2-26.
